posts.title: Savory Dokra Squares
posts.meta_description: Savory dokra squares pair semolina, yogurt, cumin and cilantro in a quick steamed-style snack with a light, tender crumb and bright finish.
posts.body_markdown:
Savory dokra squares are built from a simple semolina-and-yogurt batter, but the result depends on timing. The leavening goes in at the end, so the batter should move quickly from bowl to cooking dish.

The flavor is restrained and savory: cumin, turmeric, cilantro and lemon give the soft crumb enough definition without making the snack heavy. Green or tomato chutney works well alongside as a sharper counterpoint.

The source prepares this version in a microwave for speed. The important culinary sequence is to mix the base thoroughly, add the leavening last, cook promptly, and then let the square set before cutting.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup cream of wheat
- Salt to taste
- 1 teaspoon canola oil
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds, lightly crushed
- 1–2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 1/2 teaspoons lemon juice
- 1 cup plain yogurt
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 heaping teaspoon Eno Fruit Salt

## Method
Combine the semolina, salt, oil, turmeric, cumin, cilantro, lemon juice, yogurt and water until evenly mixed. Transfer to a shallow microwave-safe dish, quickly stir in the Eno, cover, and cook on high for about 8 minutes. Rest for at least 4 minutes before cutting into squares or diamonds. Serve warm or at room temperature with chutney.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Bhel Puris
posts.meta_description: Make crisp bhel puris from rice and spelt flours, rolled paper-thin and fried until golden for use with chutneys, chaat and tea-time snacks.
posts.body_markdown:
Bhel puris are small, crisp pastry rounds designed to carry chutneys, potatoes and other chaat toppings without disappearing under them. Their character comes from a very thin roll and an even fry.

The dough uses equal parts rice flour and spelt flour with only enough cold water to bring it together. A short rest makes the dough easier to roll, while even thickness helps each round cook at the same pace.

Frying is brief and active. Work in small batches, turn the puris as they color, and drain them well so they stay crisp. Once cooled, they can be served on their own or used as the base for bhel and chaat.

## Ingredients
- 2/3 cup rice flour
- 2/3 cup spelt flour
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 3–9 tablespoons cold water, as needed
- Vegetable oil, for deep-frying

## Method
Mix the flours and salt, then add just enough cold water to form a firm, workable dough. Knead until smooth, cover and rest for at least 30 minutes. Roll very thin, cut into roughly 2-inch rounds and keep the rounds covered with a damp towel. Fry 8–10 at a time in hot oil for 1–2 minutes, turning until golden on both sides. Drain on paper towels and cool before serving.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Bhel Indian Tea Time Snack
posts.seo_title: Bhel Indian Tea Time Snack | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A build-your-own bhel tea-time spread with puffed rice, potatoes, sprouts, chutneys, lime and puris for a crisp, tangy, highly adaptable snack.
posts.body_markdown:
Bhel works best when contrast is preserved: crisp puffed rice, tender potato, fresh herbs, sprouts, chutneys and crunchy puris all meet at the last moment. Mixing too early softens the textures that make the snack lively.

The source presents the ingredients separately so each person can build a puri to taste. That format also makes the snack easy to adjust, because heat, acidity, sweetness and crunch can be changed at the table.

For a more casual serving, combine the dry and fresh ingredients in one bowl and keep the chutneys and lime on the side. Add them just before eating so the mixture stays bright and crisp.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups puffed rice
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 tomatoes, diced
- 2 cups boiled potatoes, diced
- 3 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
- 1/2 cup fine sev
- 2 cups parboiled mung bean sprouts
- 1/4 cup crushed almonds
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- 4 tablespoons green chutney
- 4 tablespoons tamarind chutney
- Salt to taste
- 10–12 bhel puris

## Method
Arrange the puffed rice, onion, tomatoes, potatoes, cilantro, sev, sprouts, almonds, lime and chutneys in separate bowls, with the puris alongside. Let each person spoon small amounts onto a puri and season to taste. Alternatively, toss the dry and fresh ingredients together just before serving and offer lime and chutneys separately.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Puris & Chat
posts.meta_description: Crisp puris filled with potato, tamarind chutney, cumin, yogurt and chili create a compact chaat with sweet, tangy, cool and spicy contrast.
posts.body_markdown:
Puris and chat turn a crisp shell into a small layered bite. Potato gives it substance, tamarind brings sweetness and acidity, cumin adds warmth, and yogurt cools the sharper edges.

The assembly matters more than exact uniformity. Each puri should be opened gently and filled just before eating so it stays crisp rather than absorbing the sauces too early.

This is an ideal serve-at-the-table snack. Keep each component separate, let guests adjust the chili and yogurt, and build only as many puris as will be eaten immediately.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup boiled potatoes, cubed
- 1/2 cup tamarind chutney
- 4 teaspoons whole cumin seeds, toasted
- 3 fresh green chilies, finely chopped
- 1/2 cup plain yogurt, whisked until loose
- Cayenne pepper, to taste
- 12 bhel puris

## Method
Set out all fillings in separate bowls. Gently open a small hole in each puri, then add a little potato, tamarind chutney, toasted cumin and green chili. Finish with a spoonful of yogurt and a light dusting of cayenne. Assemble only just before serving so the shells remain crisp.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Deviled Eggs with Green Chutney
posts.seo_title: Deviled Eggs with Green Chutney | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A green-chutney variation on deviled eggs, combining creamy yolks with herbs, gentle heat and a fresh cilantro finish for a compact savory bite.
posts.body_markdown:
These deviled eggs keep the familiar creamy structure but replace the usual neutral seasoning with green chutney. The result is brighter, herbier and more direct.

Because the filling is simple, the balance of mayonnaise, chutney and salt matters. Start modestly, mash until smooth, then taste before refilling the whites so the chutney supports rather than dominates the egg.

Cilantro and a small pinch of cayenne finish the dish visually and aromatically. Serve the halves chilled or cool, and keep the garnish light enough that the egg remains the center of the bite.

## Ingredients
- 4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled
- 2 teaspoons mayonnaise
- Salt to taste
- 2 teaspoons green chutney
- A few fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, for garnish

## Method
Halve the eggs lengthwise and remove the yolks. Mash the yolks with mayonnaise, salt and green chutney until smooth and creamy. Spoon the mixture back into the egg whites, then finish with chopped cilantro and a light sprinkle of cayenne. Chill until ready to serve.

posts.title: Green Chutney Cheese Toast
posts.meta_description: Green chutney cheese toast layers herb chutney and melting mozzarella over bread, then broils it until bubbling for a fast savory snack or canapé.
posts.body_markdown:
Green chutney cheese toast is less a complicated recipe than a useful assembly. The chutney supplies herbs, acidity and heat; the cheese softens those edges and turns the toast into something substantial.

Broiling is the key moment. The bread should be close enough to the heat for the cheese to bubble and color, but not so long that the edges burn before the center is ready.

Serve whole slices for a quick snack or cut them into small squares for canapés. The dish is best straight from the broiler, while the cheese is still fluid and the bread remains crisp underneath.

## Ingredients
- 4–6 slices bread
- 1–2 teaspoons green chutney per slice
- 1 thin slice mozzarella per slice

## Method
Heat the broiler. Spread each slice of bread with a thin, even layer of green chutney, then cover with mozzarella. Arrange on a baking sheet and broil until the cheese bubbles and begins to brown. Watch closely, remove promptly, and serve immediately whole or cut into small squares.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Spiced Pecans
posts.meta_description: Roasted pecans coated with coconut oil, tamari, ginger and cayenne make a crisp, savory snack with a warm finish and deep toasted-nut flavor.
posts.body_markdown:
Spiced pecans work because the seasoning arrives in layers. Coconut oil coats the nuts first, helping them roast evenly, while tamari, ginger and cayenne are added later so their flavor stays distinct.

A moderate oven gives the pecans time to toast without scorching their natural oils. Keeping them in a single layer also matters; crowded nuts steam and color unevenly.

Cool the pecans completely before storing. Their texture firms as they come to room temperature, and a sealed container keeps the roasted flavor and crispness intact.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 cup coconut oil
- 1/3 cup tamari or soy sauce
- 2 teaspoons ground ginger
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- Olive oil spray or parchment paper
- 4 cups pecans

## Method
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Melt the coconut oil. Mix tamari, ginger and cayenne separately. Spread pecans in one layer on a prepared baking sheet, coat with coconut oil and roast for about 15 minutes. Toss immediately with the tamari mixture, return to the oven for about 10 minutes, then cool completely before storing.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Spiced Almonds
posts.meta_description: Cumin-spiced almonds are coated with frothy egg white, salt and cayenne, then roasted slowly until crisp for a clean, savory tea-time snack.
posts.body_markdown:
These spiced almonds use egg white as a light binder, allowing cumin, salt and cayenne to cling without a heavy coating. The finished nuts stay crisp rather than sticky.

The oven temperature is deliberately moderate. Stirring once or twice and returning the almonds to a single layer helps them roast evenly and prevents damp pockets from forming.

The source uses blanched almonds, which give the seasoning a cleaner surface and a slightly more delicate bite. Cool them fully before sealing them away, because trapped warmth can soften the crust.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- 1 large egg white
- 2 1/2 cups blanched almonds
- Olive oil spray or parchment paper

## Method
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Mix cumin, salt and cayenne. Beat the egg white until frothy, then toss with the spice mixture and almonds. Spread in one layer on a prepared baking sheet and roast for 25–30 minutes, stirring once or twice. Cool completely before storing in a sealed container.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Can’t Beet It Salad
posts.meta_description: A beet and fennel salad with walnuts, optional goat cheese and a gingered rice-vinegar dressing, balancing earthy, crisp and tangy elements.
posts.body_markdown:
This salad is built around contrast: tender beetroot against crisp fennel, walnuts against soft vegetables, and a sharp rice-vinegar dressing against the beets' natural sweetness.

The beets are cooked only until tender, then cooled before slicing. That keeps the salad clean and structured rather than warm and soft. Goat cheese is optional, but when used it adds a creamy, salty layer.

Dress the salad just before serving so the fennel keeps its snap. The ginger in the dressing is small but important, giving the acidity a warmer edge without overwhelming the vegetables.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups beets, steamed until just tender, cooled and sliced
- 2 cups fennel bulbs, thinly sliced
- 1/3 cup walnut halves
- 1/2 cup soft goat cheese, crumbled, optional
- 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup, optional
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste

## Method
Combine the cooled beets, fennel, walnuts and goat cheese, if using, in a large bowl. Shake the olive oil, rice vinegar, optional sweetener, ginger and salt together in a jar. Pour over the salad, toss gently and serve promptly.

posts.title: Grated Beet, Carrot & Broccoli Salad
posts.seo_title: Grated Beet, Carrot & Broccoli Salad | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A raw beet, carrot and broccoli salad with sprouts, pumpkin seeds, mint and a lemony mustard dressing for crunch, color and fresh acidity.
posts.body_markdown:
This raw salad layers several kinds of crunch instead of relying on one dominant ingredient. Grated carrot and beet give color, broccoli adds firmness, and sprouts and pumpkin seeds keep the texture varied.

Mint and dried fruit provide small accents rather than turning the salad sweet. The dressing is lemon-forward, with oil, garlic and Dijon adding enough body to coat the vegetables without weighing them down.

Because the ingredients are finely cut, the salad comes together quickly. Toss gently and serve soon after dressing so the greens and sprouts stay lively.

## Ingredients
- Mixed greens for a medium salad bowl
- 1 cup sunflower seed sprouts
- 3/4 cup grated carrots
- 1/4 cup grated beets
- 1/4 cup small broccoli florets
- 1 heaping tablespoon dried cranberries
- 1 tablespoon raw pumpkin seeds
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 4 tablespoons hemp seed oil or olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, crushed
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Place the greens, sprouts, carrots, beets, broccoli, cranberries, pumpkin seeds and mint in a bowl. Shake the lemon juice, oil, garlic, Dijon, salt and pepper together until emulsified. Pour over the salad, toss lightly and serve.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Refreshing Apple Walnut Celery Salad
posts.seo_title: Refreshing Apple Walnut Celery Salad | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Crisp apple, celery, red leaf lettuce and walnuts meet a simple lemon-and-olive-oil dressing in a bright salad built around freshness and crunch.
posts.body_markdown:
This salad depends on fresh texture more than complex seasoning. Crisp apple and celery sit against soft red leaf lettuce, while walnuts bring a deeper crunch and a mild richness.

Lemon is the dominant dressing flavor. Its acidity sharpens the apples and keeps the finished salad bright; olive oil is used lightly so the ingredients stay clean rather than glossy and heavy.

Cut the apples shortly before serving and leave the peel on for color and texture. Once dressed, toss only enough to coat the leaves and bring the components together.

## Ingredients
- 6 cups red leaf lettuce, shredded
- 2 red apples, unpeeled and diced
- 2 celery stalks, sliced
- 1/2 cup walnuts, chopped
- 6 tablespoons lemon juice
- 4 tablespoons olive oil

## Method
Combine the lettuce, apples, celery and walnuts in a medium bowl. Drizzle with lemon juice and olive oil, then toss gently until evenly coated. Serve immediately while the apples and celery are still crisp.

posts.title: The Essential Green Salad
posts.meta_description: Mixed greens, avocado, cucumber, broccoli and sprouts form a simple everyday salad finished with balsamic vinegar, olive oil, salt and pepper.
posts.body_markdown:
The essential green salad is deliberately uncomplicated. Mixed greens provide the base, while avocado, cucumber, broccoli and sprouts give the bowl enough variation in texture to feel complete.

The dressing stays equally simple: balsamic vinegar, olive oil, salt and pepper. With so few ingredients, the quality and freshness of the greens and oil are more noticeable than in a heavily dressed salad.

Treat the recipe as a flexible foundation rather than a rigid formula. Seeds, raisins or grapes can add contrast, but the core works because the vegetables remain recognizable and lightly dressed.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups mixed greens
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 1 cup cucumber, sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets, chopped
- 1 cup alfalfa sprouts
- 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar
- 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Place the greens, avocado, cucumber, broccoli and sprouts in a large bowl. Drizzle with balsamic vinegar and olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss gently. Serve at once.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Pear & Pecorino Mixed Green Salad
posts.seo_title: Pear & Pecorino Mixed Green Salad | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Ripe pear, mixed greens and Pecorino meet balsamic, olive oil, basil and pepper in a salad where salty cheese sharpens the fruit's sweetness.
posts.body_markdown:
Pear and Pecorino work because each makes the other more distinct. The fruit is soft and sweet; the cheese is salty, firm and sharp. Mixed greens keep both from becoming too rich.

The pears are first coated with balsamic and a small amount of sweetener. That step seasons the fruit directly rather than asking the final dressing to do all the work.

Build the salad on individual plates if presentation matters. Thin cheese shavings, a little olive oil, black pepper and torn basil are enough to finish it without covering the pear.

## Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
- 1 teaspoon agave nectar or honey
- 3 ripe pears, sliced
- 3 cups mixed greens
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 1/2 cup Pecorino Romano shavings
- 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground pepper
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, torn

## Method
Mix the balsamic vinegar and agave or honey until smooth, then toss the pear slices in the mixture. Divide the greens among serving plates and arrange the pears on top. Drizzle with olive oil, scatter over the Pecorino, season with pepper and finish with basil.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Crunchy Broccoli Slaw
posts.meta_description: Broccoli stems, carrot and red cabbage make a crisp slaw with raisins and a tangy cider-vinegar dressing, chilled briefly so the flavors settle.
posts.body_markdown:
Broccoli stems are the point of this slaw, not a leftover to hide. Julienned finely, they have a firm, fresh crunch that stands up well to grated carrot and shredded red cabbage.

The dressing is creamy but acidic, using mayonnaise and apple cider vinegar to soften the raw vegetables without making them limp. Raisins are optional and add a restrained sweet contrast.

A short rest in the refrigerator is useful here. Thirty minutes gives the dressing time to season the vegetables while preserving the crisp structure that makes the slaw work.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups broccoli stems, julienned, tough parts removed
- 1 cup carrots, grated
- 1 cup red cabbage, finely shredded
- 1/4 cup raisins, optional
- 1/2 cup vegan mayonnaise
- 4 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
- 1/2 teaspoon salt

## Method
Combine the broccoli stems, carrots, cabbage and raisins in a medium bowl. Mix the mayonnaise, cider vinegar and salt until smooth, then fold through the vegetables. Cover and refrigerate for about 30 minutes before serving.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Broccoli & Almond Armor Salad
posts.meta_description: Broccoli, almonds, currants and red onion are tossed with a yogurt-mayonnaise dressing for a crisp, creamy salad with sweet and savory contrast.
posts.body_markdown:
This broccoli salad balances crunch, sweetness and creaminess in a compact bowl. Raw broccoli and almonds provide the firm texture, while currants soften the edges with small bursts of sweetness.

The dressing combines yogurt, mayonnaise, honey and vinegar. It is creamy enough to coat the broccoli but still has enough acidity to keep the salad from feeling heavy.

The salad improves after a little time in the refrigerator. Chilling lets the currants soften slightly and the dressing settle into the broccoli while the almonds keep their bite.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups broccoli florets
- 1/2 cup red onion, chopped
- 1/4 cup almonds, chopped
- 1/2 cup currants
- 1/2 cup plain light yogurt
- 1/4 cup light mayonnaise
- 2 tablespoons honey
- 1 tablespoon vinegar
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Toss the broccoli, red onion, almonds and currants together. In a separate bowl, mix the yogurt, mayonnaise, honey and vinegar until smooth. Fold the dressing through the salad, season with salt and pepper, and chill before serving if time allows.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Tomato, Parsley & Yellow Bell Pepper Salad
posts.seo_title: Tomato, Parsley & Yellow Bell Pepper Salad | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Tomato, parsley and yellow bell pepper form a colorful, herb-forward salad finished simply with balsamic or lemon, olive oil, salt and pepper.
posts.body_markdown:
This salad puts parsley in the bowl as an ingredient rather than a garnish. Its herbal freshness gives structure to juicy tomato and crisp yellow bell pepper.

The dressing can move in two directions: balsamic for deeper sweetness and acidity, or lemon for a brighter, cleaner finish. Either works because the vegetables themselves remain the main event.

Cut the tomato and pepper into similarly sized pieces so each serving gets the full combination. Dress just before eating to preserve the parsley's freshness and the pepper's crunch.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup tomatoes, cubed
- 2 cups fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 cup yellow bell pepper, cubed
- 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar or 3 tablespoons lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, flax oil or hemp oil
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Combine the tomato, parsley and yellow bell pepper in a medium bowl. Drizzle with balsamic vinegar or lemon juice and the oil. Season with salt and pepper, toss gently and serve.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Mediterranean Breeze Salad
posts.meta_description: Tomato, avocado, mint and green onion are dressed with lemon and olive oil in a quick Mediterranean-style salad with optional cayenne heat.
posts.body_markdown:
Mediterranean Breeze Salad is a quick combination of juicy tomato, creamy avocado and fresh mint. The contrast is simple, which is why the ingredients need to be ripe and well seasoned.

Green onion adds a light savory edge, while lemon and olive oil pull the tomato and avocado together. Cayenne is optional; a small amount gives warmth without obscuring the mint.

Because avocado softens as it sits, this salad is best assembled close to serving time. Toss gently so the pieces stay intact and the dressing coats rather than crushes them.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup tomatoes, chopped
- 1 cup avocado, chopped
- 1/4 cup packed fresh mint leaves, chopped
- 1 tablespoon green onion, minced
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, flax oil or hemp oil
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, optional

## Method
Combine the tomato, avocado, mint and green onion in a bowl. Drizzle with lemon juice and oil, then add salt and optional cayenne. Toss carefully and serve immediately.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Tomato, Feta & Mint Salad
posts.meta_description: Vine-ripened tomatoes, feta, mint and black olives are finished with lemon and olive oil, then chilled briefly for a bright, salty summer salad.
posts.body_markdown:
Tomato, feta and mint is a familiar Mediterranean combination, but the balance matters. The tomatoes bring juiciness, feta brings salt, and mint keeps the plate from becoming too rich.

Black olives deepen the savory side while lemon supplies the main acidity. Olive oil should round the salad out, not drown the tomatoes or flatten the mint.

Arrange rather than heavily toss this salad. A short chill helps the flavors meet, but it is still best served while the tomatoes retain their shape and the mint remains fresh.

## Ingredients
- 8 vine-ripened tomatoes, sliced
- 1 cup feta cheese
- 1 bunch fresh mint leaves
- 3/4 cup small black olives, pitted
- Juice of 3 lemons
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Arrange the tomato slices on a platter. Crumble the feta over them, tuck mint leaves around the tomatoes and scatter over the olives. Drizzle first with lemon juice and then olive oil, season with salt and pepper, cover and chill for about 30 minutes before serving.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Fresh Daikon & Endive Salad
posts.meta_description: Daikon, cucumber, carrot, watercress and endive are arranged raw with herbs, lemon and salt for a crisp platter built around clean bitter notes.
posts.body_markdown:
Fresh daikon and endive salad is closer to a composed raw-vegetable platter than a conventional tossed salad. The appeal is in the crisp cuts, distinct shapes and clean bitter notes.

Daikon, cucumber and carrot are cut into sticks, while watercress and endive bring leafy contrast. Dill or mint can be used as the aromatic element, depending on what suits the rest of the meal.

Seasoning stays minimal: salt and lemon juice, or rice vinegar in place of lemon. That restraint keeps the vegetables identifiable and lets the platter function as a fresh counterpoint to richer dishes.

## Ingredients
- 1 daikon, cut into 2-inch sticks
- A few sprigs fresh dill or mint
- 1 1/2 cups cucumber, cut into 2-inch sticks
- 2 cups carrots, cut into 2-inch sticks
- 1 bunch watercress
- 2 heads endive, leaves separated
- Salt to taste
- Juice of 1 lemon or 4–6 tablespoons rice vinegar

## Method
Arrange the daikon, herbs, cucumber, carrots, watercress and endive on a platter. Sprinkle lightly with salt and finish with lemon juice or rice vinegar. Serve immediately while the vegetables are crisp.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: The Dainty Cachumber
posts.meta_description: A simple Indian cachumber of onion, tomato, vinegar, chili and cilantro adds fresh acidity and gentle heat beside richer savory dishes.
posts.body_markdown:
Cachumber is a small salad with a large role at the table. Onion and tomato bring freshness, while vinegar and chili cut through richer dishes and make each bite feel sharper.

This salad is intentionally spare. There is no heavy dressing to hide behind, so the onion should be sliced cleanly, the tomatoes ripe, and the vinegar measured rather than poured freely.

Cilantro is optional but useful when you want a greener finish. Letting the salad rest briefly can soften the onion, though it should still reach the table with some crispness.

## Ingredients
- 1 onion, sliced
- 2 large tomatoes, cubed
- 3 tablespoons apple cider vinegar or rice vinegar
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper or chopped fresh green chili, optional
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, minced, optional

## Method
Combine the onion, tomatoes, vinegar, salt and optional chili in a bowl. Add cilantro if using, toss well and taste for balance. Serve immediately or chill briefly to let the flavors settle.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: The Great White Salad
posts.meta_description: Cucumber and daikon are salted, drained and dressed with rice vinegar and a touch of sweetness for a clean, crisp salad with restrained acidity.
posts.body_markdown:
The Great White Salad is built from cucumber and daikon, two ingredients that reward careful handling. Salting them first pulls out excess water and concentrates their clean, crisp texture.

Rinsing after the brief salt rest is important. It removes surface salt while preserving the change in texture, so the final dressing stays balanced rather than becoming diluted.

Rice vinegar and a small amount of sweetener form the entire dressing. After tossing, give the vegetables a short rest so the acidity can penetrate without softening them too far.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 cups cucumber, chopped
- 1 1/2 cups daikon, thinly sliced
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 6 tablespoons rice vinegar
- 2 tablespoons agave nectar or another mild sweetener

## Method
Place the cucumber and daikon in a colander, sprinkle with salt and leave over a bowl or sink for 5–10 minutes. Rinse and gently squeeze out excess water. Stir the rice vinegar and sweetener together until dissolved, toss with the vegetables, and rest for 15–30 minutes before serving.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: The Bittersweet Salad
posts.meta_description: Thin carrot and daikon slices are salted, drained and dressed with rice vinegar and mild sweetness for a crisp salad with sweet-bitter contrast.
posts.body_markdown:
The Bittersweet Salad makes one contrast do most of the work: sweet carrot against the sharper, more assertive character of daikon. Thin slicing keeps the two textures closely matched.

As with the related cucumber-and-daikon salad, a short salt rest changes the vegetables before the dressing is added. It draws off water and helps the final seasoning cling more evenly.

The dressing is only rice vinegar and a mild sweetener. Let the salad sit briefly after tossing so the flavors settle, then serve while the vegetables still have a clear snap.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup carrots, thinly sliced
- 1 1/2 cups daikon, thinly sliced
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 2 tablespoons agave nectar or another mild sweetener

## Method
Place the carrots and daikon in a colander, sprinkle with salt and rest for 5–10 minutes. Rinse, then gently squeeze out excess water. Stir the rice vinegar and sweetener together until dissolved, toss with the vegetables and let stand for 15–30 minutes before serving.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: The Cleansing Bitter Greens
posts.meta_description: Dark leaf lettuce, arugula and radicchio make a deliberately bitter salad, balanced with balsamic vinegar, olive or walnut oil, salt and pepper.
posts.body_markdown:
This bitter-greens salad is direct: dark leaf lettuce, arugula and radicchio are allowed to taste like themselves. The point is not to disguise bitterness but to balance it.

Balsamic vinegar adds acidity and a little sweetness, while olive or walnut oil softens the sharper edges. The dressing should be light enough that the leaves keep their shape and individual character.

Serve the salad beside foods with more richness or softness. Its bitter, crisp profile works best as contrast, which is why extra toppings are unnecessary.

## Ingredients
- 6 cups dark green leaf lettuce, torn
- 2 cups arugula, torn
- 1 cup radicchio, torn into small pieces
- 1/4 cup walnut oil or olive oil
- 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Combine the lettuce, arugula and radicchio in a large bowl. Drizzle with the oil and balsamic vinegar, season with salt and pepper, and toss lightly until the leaves are just coated. Serve immediately.

posts.title: The Perfect Pomegranate & Spinach Salad
posts.meta_description: Spinach, pomegranate, herbs and toasted pine nuts meet a honeyed cider-vinegar dressing in a salad balancing tart fruit, greens and crunch.
posts.body_markdown:
Pomegranate and spinach create a strong visual and textural contrast: dark leaves, bright fruit and toasted pine nuts. The salad feels complete without needing a long ingredient list.

Cilantro or parsley keeps the greens aromatic, while optional red onion adds a sharper savory note. Toasting the pine nuts matters because it gives them enough flavor to stand beside the tart fruit.

The dressing combines olive oil, apple cider vinegar and honey. Shake it until emulsified, then add only enough to coat the leaves so the pomegranate remains distinct rather than disappearing into the dressing.

## Ingredients
- 5–6 cups spinach leaves, chopped
- 1/3 cup fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped
- 1 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/3 cup pine nuts, toasted
- 1/4 cup red onion, sliced, optional
- 4 tablespoons olive oil
- 4 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
- 2 teaspoons honey
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Combine the spinach, herbs, pomegranate seeds, pine nuts and optional red onion in a large bowl. Shake the olive oil, cider vinegar, honey, salt and pepper together until blended. Pour over the salad, toss gently and serve.

posts.title: Crunchy Spinach Salad
posts.meta_description: Spinach, bell peppers, carrot, dried fruit, walnuts and optional feta are dressed with balsamic, honey, Dijon and herbs for layered crunch.
posts.body_markdown:
Crunchy Spinach Salad earns its name from several textures rather than one. Spinach forms the soft base, peppers and carrot add crispness, walnuts bring a firmer bite, and dried fruit adds chew.

Feta is optional, but a small amount adds salt and creaminess without taking over the vegetables. The dressing is fuller than a simple vinaigrette, combining balsamic, honey, Dijon, herbs and optional garlic.

Crush dried herbs between your palms before adding them; that small step releases more aroma. Dress the salad just before serving so the spinach stays fresh and the crunchy ingredients remain distinct.

## Ingredients
- 5–6 cups spinach leaves, chopped
- 1/2 cup red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 cup yellow bell pepper, diced
- 1 cup carrots, grated
- 1–2 tablespoons raisins or dried cranberries
- 2 tablespoons walnuts, chopped
- 2 tablespoons feta cheese, crumbled, optional
- 1/3 cup olive oil
- 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1 teaspoon dried basil or oregano
- 1 clove garlic, minced, optional

## Method
Combine the spinach, peppers, carrot, dried fruit, walnuts and optional feta in a large bowl. Shake the olive oil, balsamic, honey, Dijon, salt, pepper, dried herbs and optional garlic together. Pour over the salad, toss gently and serve immediately.
